text:
mike_sales: Quick sync — BankCo POC signed, needing a capacity plan + answers for a few security Qs. They expect 200 req/s baseline, 2k QPS bursts for short windows. Model is `fluent-13B` quantized. Do we recommend reserved GPUs or pooled credits? Also Q12 in the security questionnaire asks about KMS key rotation and HSM usage.

priya_se: Congrats! :tada: For this profile I'd lean reserved + small burst credits. Reserved for predictable baseline (200 rps) and credits to cover spikes to 2k. Helps with billing predictability and SLA.

alex_sa: Agree on reserved baseline. Quick math: assume avg tokens/request ~120 (prompt+response). At 200 rps -> 24k tokens/s. At 2k -> 240k tokens/s. On an A100/4GPU-like pool with quantized model we estimate ~40k tokens/s per GPU (w/ batching + KV cache). So baseline needs ~1 GPU, safe reserve 2 GPUs for headroom and AZ failover. Burst credits cover the rest.

ben_sre: Notes on autoscale/fallback: recommended policy: keep 2 reserved devices in the reservation, allow autoscale to add burst GPUs from shared pool up to 8 GPUs with a 30s cool-down. If burst unavailable, route to fallback model `fluent-7B-quant` (lower cost/latency) automatically. Also prewarm KV cache during preheat window to avoid cold-start token spikes.

alex_sa: Pasting a sample autoscale fragment we can give presales (not exhaustive):

```
autoscale:
  reserved: 2
  max_burst: 8
  scale_cooldown_sec: 30
  preheat_window_sec: 90
  eviction_tolerance: 0.2   # allow 20% slot eviction for spot-backed burst
  fallback_model: "fluent-7B-quant"
```

priya_se: Pricing question from sales: how do credits get consumed vs reserved billing? We should give a clear example for them.

mike_sales: Yes please — they want to see a monthly cost example and what invoice spikes look like during sustained high usage.

ben_sre: Example (ballpark): Reserved 2 GPUs = fixed monthly SKU. Burst credits consumed per-token when additional GPUs used; if credits exhausted, autoscale will still try to allocate burst GPUs billed at on-demand rates (higher). Recommend adding buffer credits for first month of POC.

julia_sec: On the sec questionnaire Q12: KMS rotation — we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS with automatic rotation enabled. For HSM, we integrate with external HSM via KMIP for Private deployments; public Hosted customers can opt for envelope encryption with our KMS and rotate CMKs on customer schedule. I can draft a short paragraph for the questionnaire.

mike_sales: Can you add that paragraph here, JulIa? Also customer asked about audit logs for key access and model access.

julia_sec: Draft: "Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys with rotation and audit logging. For Private deployments we support direct HSM integration (KMIP) and provide Key Access logs to the customer's audit stream. Access to plaintext is never stored in logs; only key usage events are recorded with timestamps and principal ids." Feel free to tweak.

priya_se: Action items: 1) Alex — finalize GPU count + fallback latencies (eta EOD). 2) Ben — recommended autoscale YAML + preheat schedule (eta tomorrow). 3) Julia — finalize Q12 answer + where to point them for compliance docs (eta EOD). 4) Mike — I'll prepare a cost example with reserved+credit scenarios and a 30-day buffer suggestion.

alex_sa: On it. One more note: suggest enabling prefix/KV caching for their chat workload and instrument token distribution during the 48h smoke test so we can refine billing estimates quickly.

deploy-bot: [deploy] presales/smoke-test: started job 5123 for project bankco-poc — will run 2h synthetic load at 200rps and 5x spike tests.

mike_sales: Perfect — thanks team. I'll share this thread with the customer and attach the sample autoscale snippet + Julia's wording.

priya_se: :thumbsup:
